header.running_head: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Consults with Men of knowledge

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Atiyya bin Bilaal and Hadhrat Sahm bin Minjaab
blocks.text: reply of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was one that engendered unity). [^1]
Consultation with the Sahabah (RA) in Battle

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once wrote to Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) saying, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to consult in matters of war, so ensure that you do the same." [^2]
A narration of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abi Awfa (RA) has already passed discussing the consultation of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) with men of knowledge before engaging the Romans in battle. [^3]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) Consults with Men of knowledge
Hadhrat Umar (RA) Informs his Consultative Assembly about his Proposal to the Daughter of Hadhrat Ali (RA)

Hadhrat Abu Ja'far narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) requested Hadhrat Ali (RA) for his daughter Ummu Kulthoom's hand in marriage. Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "I had intended to marry all my daughters only to the sons of Ja'far." To this, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "O Ali! Marry her to me because I swear by Allaah that there is no other person on earth who anticipates as much as I do by treating her well (this he explains later)." Hadhrat Ali (RA) then agreed to let Hadhrat Umar (RA) marry his daughter. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then approached the gathering of Muhaajireen who always sat in the Masjid between the grave of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the pulpit. They included Hadhrat Ali (RA), Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), Hadhrat Zubayr (RA), Talha (RA) and Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA). Whenever any matter presented itself to him from far off places, Hadhrat Umar (RA) would always inform the members of this gathering and then seek their opinions about the matter.
This time he came to them and said, "Congratulate me on my new marriage!" They all congratulated him and then asked, "Who did you marry, O Ameerul Mu'mineen?" "The daughter of Ali bin Abi Taalib," he replied. He then started to explain, "Indeed Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Every connection and relation shall be severed on the day of Qiyaamah except my connections and my relations.' I had been a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ and now I wish to become his relative as well." [^4]
Sayf and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.390).
Tabraani, narrating from reliable sources, as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.5 Pg.319). Bazzaar and Uqayli have also reported the narration authentically, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.163).

This narration is found under the heading "Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Ensures that Armies are Dispatched in the Path of Allaah. He Encourages the Muslims to March in Jihaad and Consults with the Sahabah (RA) About Fighting the Romans" and the subheading "Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Consults with the Senior Sahabah (RA) Concerning a Military Offensive Against the Romans and Delivers a Speech in this Regard".
Ibn Sa'd, Sa'eed bin Mansoor and Ibn Rahway in brief, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.98).
